definition: One whole recording per listed meaning for Walter in game review, SRS/explanations, opening recall/preview, puzzle guidance and finite operational states. Lessons are deferred. Exact dynamic SAN, squares, scores and names stay written. Count is this explicit catalogue, not a universal minimum, current automatic output count or finite verbatim narration of every possible string.

policy.scope: Owner-approved non-lesson Walter bank: game review, SRS/explanations, opening recall/preview, puzzle guidance and finite operational states. Lessons remain deferred. Selecting a recording still requires the current authorized surface and supporting facts.
policy.defaults: Four transient/defensive states remain silent and unrecorded. The bank contains 181 recordings; presence of a recording never authorizes hidden, cold-answer, stale or automatic playback.
policy.game: Retain family-specific gates and exact selected claim identity from walter-dialogue-inventory.json. The 21 secondary scripts require explicit secondary-surface policy; do not silently narrate hidden popovers.
practice: practiceIntent accepts only authorized API feedback; cold cards cannot use future frames, summary, grade, source-game findings or expression as answer hints.
explain_review requires an attempt belonging to this session or completed session before solution access. No pre-answer narration.
No success narration on reveal or restored GET feedback. User-invoked replay may narrate existing evidence, but must not emit a fresh grading reward.
Scope selection to current session, attempt, analysis and exact frame/finding. Cancel on retry, navigation, hide/unmount and coach change. Current error/pending state suppresses stale chess claims.

Current public fields are insufficient for reliable new selectors in some cases: frame lacks explicit promotion/castling/checkmate/escaped-check facts, summary is plain prose, and finding rule IDs collapse some detailed branches. Future producer-side structured speech projection is required; do not parse arbitrary text or infer grading from expressions.

Existing game clip reuse is a new factual mapping, not direct use of the current game-only gate. In SRS the exact attempted line is authoritative; accepted Finding.direction=missed_opportunity means opportunity found in this answer, not a missed move.
Whole-frame combinations retain capture, promotion and king state together; no need for separate actor/target/promoted-piece pronunciation files because those exact identities stay written.

Detailed finding variants retain concrete mechanisms and stated material outcomes. Generic motif recordings are used only where the producer itself presents no stronger distinctive mechanism or outcome.
otherSurfaces: Puzzle outcomes require separate rejected, accepted-next, clean solved, failed-then-solved, and revealed recordings; none is objectively Best.

Opening recall acceptance means membership in snapshot selected repertoire. Main coach body deliberately uses the same neutral accepted line regardless of an earlier failure; relearning outcome remains in separate receipt.
Opening recall errors share the exact same useReviewSession gradingError producer as SRS, so srs-practice-error can be reused without losing authority or recovery semantics.
Puzzle errors require reload, unlike review retry. Do not reuse the SRS try-again script for their errors.
Recorded clips must retain user action/restored-state policy; listing a visible message does not authorize automatic replay on GET/load.
These are exact counts of this auditable script design, not a mathematical minimum across all possible wording designs.
policy.lesson: Deferred by owner. Do not generate course narration, hints, game notes, reveal narration or fixed lesson guidance. Adding or editing courses must not require maintaining this voice pack. Existing written lessons and lesson behavior remain unchanged.
policy.wording: Use complete reusable explanations of supported ideas. Exact moves, squares, evaluations and identities remain written. Text-character counts are exact draft input sizes, not billed credits or guaranteed take counts.
policy.narration: One or more complete supported sentences may be presented explicitly; this is not chopped-word assembly. Repetition alternatives, emotional retakes, localization and other coaches are not multiplied into the count.
policy.generation: The owner authorized completing Walter after approving the Older teacher voice and automatic mouth generator. Reuse the eight unchanged contrast recordings; generate the remaining 173 once in nine bounded plans of at most 20 requests. No lesson recordings.

counts.frameSemantics: 16 noncastle combinations + 3 castle combinations + 1 original position; two reuse existing recordings.

routes.behavior: Error first; cold/retry without feedback; then detail = preview frame.annotation || feedback.explanation_summary || feedback.message || study fallback. recovered/accepted/explanation/retry select delivery. Rejected feedback outside preview uses retry and discards detail by existing template; no additional backend retry-message recording is currently spoken.
Primary selected frame.annotation; optional secondary data.summary if distinct and fits maxClaims/maxCharacters. Frame and summary are independent supported meanings, not one generic Good job.
Selected finding.explanation and its exact skill cue. These are visible outside DialogueText and would need an explicit speech action/surface policy.
Five finite semantic note families plus arbitrary accepted manual exercise explanation. Engine version is metadata.

Current report.board_cues.caption combines legal-reply prefix or frame1 annotation with optional selected finding.explanation. review_cues requires a finding frame_ply <=2; unavailable later findings do not create extra game Show why output. SRS can select every emitted finding.
Non-coach UI is enumerated separately and is not silently included in semantic dialogue recording count.
No Walter/ReviewCoach/DialogueText. Classification prose and JSON audit remain audit UI, including historical arbitrary text; not folded into coach speech.

method: Read AGENTS.md, docs/AUDIO.md, prior 92-script inventory and its README.
Traced actual JSX branch precedence and server feedback producers without running engines/tests or provider requests.
Counted every concrete currently emitted message form; composed opening rejection messages have three finite server-backed variants.
Reusable spoken summaries omit dynamic study names, moves and UI badges. Do not claim a finite verbatim bank for arbitrary metadata or future authored content.
One whole complete spoken recording per documented meaning, with same-authority SRS error reuse explicitly identified; no speculative extra wordings/takes.
Read actual gameIntent branch precedence, Walter storyteller wording, composition strategy, renderDialogue fallback, PositionCoach body and ReviewExplanation body.
Count exact currently visible finite strings after Walter composition, not every template fragment or computed-but-hidden utterance.
The five ordinary forms are guaranteed when their documented branch is selected. The renderer fallback is a real defensive output but is not established as a reachable normal valid-report state.
No engines, provider calls, tests, database inspection or changes to tracked source. Each text is a proposed whole recording; current automatic-speech eligibility remains unchanged.

boundariesAndExclusions.reason: User-authored string up to 5000 characters, exposed in ReviewDetails and accepted curated explanation notes. There is no repository-wide finite authored corpus to count. Supporting arbitrary future text requires authoring another recording or retaining text; generic acknowledgment does not cover its reason.
Open-ended compatibility text if a legacy report lacks intelligence. Preserve exact written evidence; no fabricated mapping from prose.
Non-dialogue Notice surfaces with arbitrary transport/domain error message, not a chess explanation.

Three fixed loading/checking states are included in operational scripts and recommended silent via deferredIds. Headings, button labels, scheduling receipts and metadata are excluded from coach dialogue.

SRS explanation producers do not emit material_loss, missed_material_gain, allowed_mate, missed_mate, opponent_threat_recognition or trapped_piece findings. Game Show why can emit opponent_threat_recognition but does not render its cue.

Try again. This practice attempt is saved. and Try again. Your first attempt has been recorded; take your time. are not exposed by Walter retry template, which ignores detail; no extra recording counted merely because backend strings exist.
Optional observation/takeaway prose does not add a chess meaning; factual detail retains summary/frame script. Alternate delivery and fully verbatim complete-bubble permutations are not included.

boundariesAndExclusions.disposition: Visible coach-body study-identification metadata; keep written. Arbitrary catalogue/import/custom names have no fixed finite verbatim bank; zero extra semantic-summary scripts.

Not unrestricted in current opening recall production. Rejected branch is one base message plus zero or one of two finite non_scheduling_reason strings. Accepted/revealed branch overrides this field with frontend copy.

All lesson narration is deferred by owner for maintainability: current and future authored passages, hints, feedback, game notes, reveals and fixed lesson guidance. Historical count and exact source audit are available in commit 054cd80; they are outside this active plan.

boundariesAndExclusions.body: errorAtPosition is displayed in an inline Notice inside ReviewCoach, after DialogueText.
boundariesAndExclusions.handling: Unrestricted runtime error text. Preserve visually; no exact finite prerecorded coverage count. The game-unavailable clip may describe its own adapter state only and does not cover the Notice verbatim.

boundariesAndExclusions.body: Raw error message replaces loading/explanation paragraph in the ReviewCoach body.
boundariesAndExclusions.handling: Unrestricted runtime error text. Preserve visually; do not invent one generic error recording and call it complete coverage.

boundariesAndExclusions.body: Learner report lacking intelligence emits compatibility with report.coach || report.reason, wrapped by Walter.
boundariesAndExclusions.handling: Unrestricted historical/freeform text. The two no-report compatibility status clips do not cover this path.

Seven abbreviated claim meanings are already in the 92-script game bank. The additional humanInsightExplanation paragraphs and provider/confidence/source notes are UI help outside the coach's dialogue text and excluded by the chosen coach-dialogue scope, not silently claimed as narrated.
No current production emitter. They add no current operational recording; ordinary branches use the game claim families.

boundariesAndExclusions.reason: Buttons, headings, badges, toasts, scheduling receipts, account/settings copy and provenance/help are not counted as coach dialogue. This is not a screen-reader narration inventory.

Arbitrary scores, names, moves, PGN/user-authored commentary and legacy explanations cannot all be prerecorded verbatim. Unsupported or missing semantic mapping remains written; a generic acknowledgment is not complete spoken coverage of its reasoning.

scripts.text: The idea is a fork in this continuation. One piece attacks several targets at once.
This move allows a fork in the continuation. One opposing piece attacks several targets at once.
The stronger continuation had a fork. This move misses the chance for one piece to attack several targets at once.
The continuation uses a pin. Moving the pinned piece off the line would expose its king.
This move allows a pin in the continuation. Moving the pinned piece off the line would expose its king.
The stronger continuation used a pin. Moving the pinned piece off the line would expose its king.
The continuation uses a skewer. Moving the front piece exposes a piece behind it.
This move allows a skewer in the continuation. Moving the front piece exposes a piece behind it.
The stronger continuation had a skewer. Moving the front piece would expose a piece behind it.
The continuation removes a defender by capture. Notice what loses protection when that defender disappears.
This move allows the other side to capture a defender in the continuation. Notice what loses protection when that defender disappears.
The stronger continuation captured a defender. That was the chance to remove protection from what it was guarding.
The continuation ends in checkmate on the back rank. The king's own pieces take away escape squares.
This move allows a back-rank checkmate in the continuation. The king's own pieces take away escape squares.
The stronger continuation ended in a back-rank checkmate. This move lets that finish go.
The continuation includes a pawn promotion. Follow the pawn all the way to its last rank.
This move allows the opposing pawn to promote in the continuation. Follow that pawn all the way to its last rank.
The stronger continuation included a pawn promotion. This move misses that opportunity.
The continuation uses a discovered attack. Moving one piece opens an attacking line for another.
This move allows a discovered attack in the continuation. Moving one opposing piece opens an attacking line for another.
The stronger continuation used a discovered attack. Moving one piece would open an attacking line for another.
The continuation creates two attacks at once. Watch how the two attacking pieces work together.
This move allows two attacks at once in the continuation. Watch how the two attacking pieces work together.
The stronger continuation created two attacks at once. This move misses that chance to combine the threats.
The continuation uses a deflection. A defender is drawn away, opening a tactical opportunity.
This move allows a deflection in the continuation. An opposing move draws a defender away, opening a tactical opportunity.
The stronger continuation used a deflection. Drawing a defender away would open a tactical opportunity.
The continuation captures an undefended piece. Keep an eye on loose pieces; they can offer a straightforward opportunity.
The stronger continuation captured an undefended piece. This move misses that chance, so give loose enemy pieces a careful look.
This move allows the other side to capture an undefended piece in the continuation. Loose pieces deserve a careful look.
This move takes away a piece's only effective defender. The other side can capture that piece in the continuation.
The opponent's previous move enabled this attack. This move leaves the threat unanswered, and the piece can be captured in the continuation.
This capture invites a recapture of a more valuable piece. Count both sides of the exchange before judging the first capture.
This develops a minor piece from its original square. Notice its new place in the position.
The unplayed alternative would develop a minor piece from its original square. Notice where it would go.
This leaves a rook on an open file. There are no pawns of either color on that file.
The unplayed alternative would leave a rook on an open file. That file would contain no pawns of either color.
This leaves a rook on a semi-open file. There are no friendly pawns on that file, but at least one enemy pawn remains.
The unplayed alternative would leave a rook on a semi-open file, with no friendly pawns on that file but at least one enemy pawn.
This leaves a passed pawn: no enemy pawn is ahead on its file or either neighboring file.
The unplayed alternative would leave a passed pawn, with no enemy pawn ahead on its file or either neighboring file.
This advances a pawn that was already passed. Keep its new square in view as you compare continuations.
The unplayed alternative would advance a pawn that was already passed. Keep its new square in view as you compare continuations.
This leaves an isolated pawn, with no friendly pawn on either neighboring file.
The unplayed alternative would leave an isolated pawn, with no friendly pawn on either neighboring file.
This gives a piece support. A defender is now in place.
The unplayed alternative would give a piece support. A defender would then be in place.
This leaves a piece undefended. That alone does not mean the piece can be won.
The unplayed alternative would leave a piece undefended. That alone would not mean the piece could be won.
This opens a legal flight square the king did not have before. Compare the positions to see what opened the way.
The unplayed alternative would open a legal flight square for the king. Compare the positions to see what would open the way.
This castles the king and relocates the rook. Follow both pieces when comparing the positions.
The unplayed alternative would castle the king and relocate the rook. Follow where both pieces would go.
This capture breaks up a bishop pair. The side losing the bishop no longer has one bishop on each square color.
The unplayed alternative would capture one bishop from an opposite-colored pair, breaking up that bishop pair.
This leaves doubled pawns in the resulting position. At least two pawns of the same color share a file.
The unplayed alternative would leave doubled pawns in the resulting position, with at least two pawns of the same color sharing a file.
This move allows a forced checkmate. Follow the continuation to see why the defense can no longer hold.
There was a forced checkmate in the stronger continuation. This move lets that finish go.
The sacrifice holds up in the search even when it is accepted. Taking the offered material does not refute the idea in this line.
This was the only move we found that kept the position playable. The other moves we checked were losing.
This was the only move we found that kept the advantage. The other moves we checked were losing.
The other side has an immediate capture in reply. Follow the continuation to see which piece can be taken.
The strongest reply gives check. The continuation begins by making the king answer that threat.
The engine prefers another move here. Compare its continuation with the move that was played.
This move gives up some of the position's value compared with the engine's best continuation. Follow the reply to see how the position changes.
This preserves nearly all that the engine's best move offered. A sound choice can matter without changing the whole game.
This keeps most of the position's value, close to the stronger continuations. It is a sound way to carry the game forward.
The human-move model sees this as a natural choice, but the engine finds a stronger move. That contrast is worth studying.
The human-move model treats this as an unusual choice, and the engine still finds it strong.
The engine found one move that kept the position playable, and the model evidence suggests it was difficult to find.
The human-move model and the alternatives suggest this was a hard move to find. Keep this idea in mind for similar positions.
This move kept the position playable. The human-move model and the searched alternatives suggest it was a hard resource to find.
The human-move model sees this as a natural choice, and it is also the engine's best move.
The human-move model sees this as a natural choice. It is strong, although the engine prefers another move.
The recorded clock shows there was little time left before this move.
The recorded clock shows a quick move with time still available.
A substantial amount of recorded time went into this move.

Here the game first steps beyond the line recognized by our opening book.
After the earlier setback, this move restores a playable position. There is a way forward again.
This restores a playable position after the earlier setback. Errors by the other side helped make that recovery possible.
This makes use of the chance the opponent offered on the previous move.
The opponent's previous move offered a chance, but this move lets it pass. Compare the stronger continuation.
This same issue has appeared before in the reviewed moves of this game. Compare the examples and look for the common warning sign.
A piece left unguarded earlier has support again. Compare the two positions to see how its protection changed.
This is one of several small concessions that have worsened the position together. Look at the sequence, as well as this move.
The reviewed moves kept the advantage through to the recorded win. Follow that stretch to see how the advantage was preserved.
This issue also appears in other saved games. It is worth revisiting those examples alongside this one.
